trend_id: agentic-payments-velocity-2026 (x402/MPP settlement growth — Tier A ledger facts; stage-1 scout intel had not landed at time of pitch)
rationale: The agentic-payments story is a velocity story: rails got faster, settlement got cheaper, ~100M x402 payments cleared on Base. None of that changed what a dollar can do at one time. That is a margin-architecture problem, not a payments problem — which makes this trend a capital-efficiency read before it is anything else. And the strongest thing Vanna owns here is not a slogan, it is an inequality anyone can check.

posts.body:
Velocity is not efficiency.

~100M x402 payments have settled on Base. Money now moves at machine speed.

It still does one job at a time. Your $10,000 is three tabs, three health factors, three liquidation prices — and a gain on one leg can't back a loss on another.
thread:
Vanna's borrow guard is one inequality:

(C + B) / (D + B) ≥ 1.1

Borrowed capital never leaves the margin account, so the risk engine counts B on both sides. Start at D = 0:

C + B ≥ 1.1B → C ≥ 0.1B → B ≤ 10C

10× isn't a dial. It's what falls out of a 1.1 floor.

Which also tells you where not to sit.

At B = 10C the health factor is exactly 1.1 — the liquidation threshold itself. The ceiling is a boundary, not an operating point.

The maths is public because it's derivable. How far under it you run is your call.

One account. One health factor. Collateral that backs every leg at once instead of one leg each.

Live on Stellar testnet with Blend, Aquarius and Soroswap — XLM and USDC. Mainnet addresses publish at launch.

Read the maths. Tell us where the risk engine is wrong.
